# Iddhipāda Saṁyutta (SN 51)

**ID:** SN 51
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Iddhipāda Saṁyutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Linked Discourses on the Bases of Psychic Power
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/sn51
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul6.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Iddhipāda Saṁyutta* (SN 51) is the fifty-first collection of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, situated within the *Mahāvagga* (Great Chapter) among the core collections dealing with the thirty-seven qualities that contribute to awakening (*bodhipakkhiyā dhammā*) [Gethin 2008]. The saṁyutta contains 86 discourses addressing the four bases of spiritual power or accomplishment (*iddhipāda*): desire or enthusiasm (*chanda*), energy (*viriya*), consciousness or mind (*citta*), and investigation (*vīmaṁsā*), each developed together with concentration (*samādhi*) and formative striving (*padhāna-saṅkhāra*) [SuttaCentral; Bodhi 2003; Gethin 2001; Hazra 1994]. While the higher purpose of the Buddhist path is liberation and arahantship, the discourses explain that developing meditative immersion through these four bases can yield both supernormal powers (*iddhi*) and supreme knowledge; past, present, and future ascetics and brahmins, including the Buddha himself, achieve spiritual mastery through them [SuttaCentral; Bodhi 2003].

Individual discourses analyze the cultivation of the four bases, including practices such as the perception of light [Sujato 2012]. In the *Vibhaṅga Sutta* (SN 51.13), a line-by-line definition of the stock formula is provided, which is nearly identical to the Suttanta analysis in the *Iddhipādavibhaṅga* (Vb 9) of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Nyanatiloka 1957; Gethin 2001; DharmaNexus]. The textual structure of the collection—pairing concise instructional teachings with detailed analytical vibhaṅgas—also provides a key comparative reference for the redaction of neighboring collections such as the *Satipaṭṭhāna Saṁyutta* [Sujato 2012].

Pali-internal text reuse identified by DharmaNexus links SN 51 extensively with the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16) and the *Āyusaṅkhārossajjana Sutta* (Ud 6.1) regarding the teaching that cultivating the four bases enables one to live for a cosmic aeon (*kappa*) [DharmaNexus; Gethin 2001], as well as with discourses in AN 3, AN 4, AN 5, AN 8, and AN 10 [DharmaNexus]. In non-Pali corpora, SuttaCentral identifies an established parallel between SN 51.15 and *Saṁyuktāgama* discourse SĀ 561 [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus additionally aligns passages of SN 51 with Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* texts (T 99), Sanskrit texts including the *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra*, *Divyāvadāna*, *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, and Harivarman's *Tattvasiddhiśāstra*, and Tibetan translations from the *Vinayakṣudrakavastu* and Abhidharma commentaries [DharmaNexus].
